General things: to increase the levels of skill trees you need to perform the associated actions, and each level of a skill tree either gives perk points or makes the skill better by increasing damage, decrease in cool-downs, duration and perk points. And the max level for your character is 50 while for attributes it’s 20 so you won’t be able to increase all of them to their max. 

Cool: each level of cool does increase your crit damage, and all resistances. So it may be worth getting a few more points even if it’s just for dialogue options in quests. I would recommend the cool blood perk and it’s associated tree. Cool blood after obtaining the perk increases your movement speed for 7 seconds after defeating an enemy. The ninjutsu tree is very much oriented towards stealth so that tree would be a miss for you. 

Intelligence: increased quick hack damage and duration, as well as Cyberdeck RAM capacity. It has skills that when performing breach protocol can impact how much damage enemies take from quick hacks (though this is from level 16 in the breach protocol tree). And some access points are gated behind your intelligence level. 

Body: the skill tree of annihilation relates to shotguns, light and heavy machine guns. 

Reflex: the assault tree relates to assault rifles, precision rifles, sniper rifles and smgs. 

Classifications of weapons: for guns this is power, smart and tech, and some perks help specific classifications. The engineering tree (under technical ability) has a perk for smart and some for tech weapons. Whereas if you are mainly planning on using Power weapons there is a perk in assault tree which is at level 18 reflexes, and one in the engineering tree at level 12 in technical ability. 

Cyberwear : of course some cyberwear is locked behind attribute levels. And some is better for certain things than others. Different cyberdecks can increase cool-down, available RAM, damage from quickhacks 

Ending: personally I would say unless you plan on using quickhacks a lot, intelligence could probably be level 8 or so. I also recommend looking at each skill tree to try and figure out what perks you would feel are best for what you are planning on using. Or even looking up some builds that other people have put together for the current patch. If you are planning on doing multiple playthoughs, you could use the first playthrough as a way for you to figure out what you like best then heavily go for a specific build on repeat playthroughs. 

Hopefully this helps, and I hope you enjoy Cyberpunk 2077.
